newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's foreign sales unaffected by scare.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's foreign sales unaffected by scare.

text.p: McDonald's Corp sales in Europe and Japan have not been affected by the "mad cow" scare in Europe or the outbreak of food poisoning in Japan, said Richard Starmann, McDonald's senior vice president of communications.
"It hasn't affected our business," he said during an address at the Texas Cattle Feeders Convention here.
In Japan, government officials suspect contaminated radish sprouts caused this summer's food poisoning outbreak that resulted in some deaths and widespread illnesses.
U.S. meat has not been linked to the outbreak in Japan, but U.S. meat industry officials have said the poisonings did cause an overall drop in food consumption.
Starmann said some individual McDonald's restaurants may have noticed a drop in sales but overall sales in Europe as well as Japan, have not been affected.

The announcement earlier this year of a suspected link between Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), also known as "mad cow" disease in the United Kingdom and a degenerative brain disease in humans curbed beef consumption in Europe. Starmann told reporters McDonalds buys beef in areas free of the bovine disease.
"We are really not a part of that story," he said in reference to the "mad cow" issue.

In the United States, Starmann said sales of the new Arch Deluxe hamburger are better than expected. The company estimated more than 85 million lbs of beef this year will go into Arch Deluxe sandwiches.
Also, he said McDonald's total 1996 beef usage should exceed 1995's 730 million lbs.
